The speech-to-song illusion

Source: R/data.R
speech_to_song.Rd

86 English listeners each hear six spoken sentences, each repeated eight times. Before the repetitions they rate how song-like the sentence sounds (1 = clearly speech, 8 = clearly song). During the repetitions they press a button as soon as the speech turns into song, and afterwards they rate the sentence again. Each sentence comes in a baseline version, a version with flattened pitch within syllables and a version with lengthened sonorous parts. Both manipulations make the illusion more likely, while musical aptitude does not. Listeners with weaker beat perception hear the song earlier, and listeners with better melody perception rate it as more song-like. For mixed logistic and ordinal models, and for a response that is missing by design.

Usage

speech_to_song

Format

A tibble with 516 rows and 9 columns:

listener

Listener ID, L01 to L86.

bat

Beat perception score (z-score), as from the Computerised Adaptive Beat Alignment Test.

mpt

Melody perception score (z-score), as from the Mistuning Perception Test.

sentence

Sentence, S1 to S9.

manipulation

Version of the sentence: "baseline", "pitch" (pitch movements within syllables flattened) or "duration" (sonorous parts lengthened by 20% and obstruents shortened by the same amount).

rating_before

Rating before the repetitions, 1 (clearly speech) to 8 (clearly song).

transformed

1 if the listener reported the illusion, 0 if not.

cycle

Repetition, 1 to 8, during which the listener reported the illusion. NA when there was no illusion.

rating_after

Rating after the repetitions, on the same scale.

Source

data-raw/speech_to_song.R

Details

True model: each listener hears two sentences in each condition, assigned in a Latin square. transformed is Bernoulli with logit -0.9 + 1.04 * pitch + 0.78 * duration plus listener (SD 1) and sentence (SD 0.5) effects. cycle and both ratings come from ordered probit models. For cycle the latent value is 0.61 * bat plus a listener effect (SD 0.6). For rating_after it is 0.2 + 1.2 * pitch + 0.91 * duration + 0.44 * mpt + 0.8 * transformed plus listener (SD 0.7) and sentence effects. The two aptitude scores correlate at about 0.5. The design and the effects of the manipulations and of aptitude follow Rathcke and Smit (2025); in their data the manipulated stimuli transformed about half of the time. The other intercepts, the effect of transformed on the final rating and all data are simulated.

References

Rathcke, T. & Smit, E. A. (2025). Musical aptitude moderates ease and vividness but not frequency of the speech-to-song illusion. Scientific Reports, 15, 33315. doi:10.1038/s41598-025-18612-8

Falk, S., Rathcke, T. & Dalla Bella, S. (2014). When speech sounds like music. Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance, 40(4), 1491-1506. doi:10.1037/a0036858

Rathcke, T., Falk, S. & Dalla Bella, S. (2024). Why does speech sometimes sound like song? Exploring the role of music-related priors in the "speech-to-song illusion". Music & Science, 7. doi:10.1177/20592043241266060

Examples

round(tapply(speech_to_song$transformed, speech_to_song$manipulation, mean), 2)
#> baseline    pitch duration 
#>     0.28     0.49     0.41 
table(speech_to_song$cycle)
#> 
#>  1  2  3  4  5  6  7  8 
#> 30 48 55 27 17 12  6  9 
wilcox.test(speech_to_song$rating_after, speech_to_song$rating_before, paired = TRUE)
#> 
#> 	Wilcoxon signed rank test with continuity correction
#> 
#> data:  speech_to_song$rating_after and speech_to_song$rating_before
#> V = 89096, p-value < 2.2e-16
#> alternative hypothesis: true location shift is not equal to 0
#> 
if (requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE)) {
  m <- lme4::glmer(transformed ~ manipulation + bat + mpt + (1 | listener) + (1 | sentence),
                   data = speech_to_song, family = binomial)
  round(lme4::fixef(m), 2)
}
#>          (Intercept)    manipulationpitch manipulationduration 
#>                -1.05                 1.03                 0.66 
#>                  bat                  mpt 
#>                 0.13                -0.13 
if (requireNamespace("ordinal", quietly = TRUE)) {
  m <- ordinal::clm(factor(rating_after) ~ manipulation + bat + mpt, data = speech_to_song,
                    link = "probit")
  print(round(coef(m)[c("manipulationpitch", "manipulationduration", "bat", "mpt")], 2))
  m <- ordinal::clm(factor(cycle) ~ bat + mpt, data = speech_to_song, link = "probit")
  print(round(coef(m)[c("bat", "mpt")], 2))
}
#>    manipulationpitch manipulationduration                  bat 
#>                 1.06                 0.61                -0.08 
#>                  mpt 
#>                 0.38 
#>  bat  mpt 
#> 0.37 0.23
